title: English Tenses Chart
content:
## English Tenses Chart

Review the simple, continuous, perfect and perfect continuous forms in present, past and future tenses.

### Lesson focus

1. Present simple: I play.
2. Present continuous: I am playing.
3. Present perfect: I have played.
4. Present perfect continuous: I have been playing.
5. Past simple: I played.
6. Past continuous: I was playing.
7. Past perfect: I had played.
8. Past perfect continuous: I had been playing.
9. Future simple: I shall/will play.
10. Future continuous: I shall/will be playing.
11. Future perfect: I shall/will have played.
12. Future perfect continuous: I shall/will have been playing.

### Understand the pattern

Use the forms as a map of time and aspect, not a list of interchangeable endings. Simple forms can describe facts or completed events; continuous forms view an action in progress; perfect forms connect one time with an earlier event; perfect continuous forms emphasise duration.

### Worked answers and explanation

Present perfect: I have played twice this week, a period still continuing. Past perfect: I had played before the rain began, placing the game before another past event. Future perfect: I will have played by noon, looking back from a future point. In these classroom labels, will expresses future time; English can express future meanings in other ways too.

### Try another

Choose the form for an action in progress at six yesterday: I ___ chess. (play)

### Suggested answer

Was playing. Was/were + -ing is past continuous. Had played would instead place the game before a later past reference point.
